summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1/node2/node3 (CentOS Stream 10). Configured node1 as initial primary with node2 and node3 as async standbys via pg_basebackup, replication over scram-sha-256 auth with a role generated on-node and injected only via secret_env. Demonstrated failover: stopped node1 (simulated primary loss), promoted node2 with pg_promote(), verified zero committed-data loss, repointed node3 to stream from node2, and rebuilt node1 as a standby of the new primary node2 via pg_basebackup (pg_rewind was unusable since data_checksums/wal_log_hints were off). Final topology: node2 = writable primary, node1 and node3 = standbys, matching the required "recovered former primary rejoins as standby of current primary" behavior. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last): captured boot_id + service health baseline, issued systemctl reboot with backgrounded ack, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed on every node, and verified PostgreSQL/replication/data fully recovered after each restart, ending with full 3-node cluster health and quorum.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 and opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on node1, node2, node3
Populated /etc/hosts cluster mapping on all nodes
Initialized node1 as primary: postgresql.conf (listen_addresses, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots, hot_standby) and pg_hba.conf entries for replicator over the cluster subnet
Generated a random replication password on node1 and created the 'replicator' role, injecting the secret only via secret_env (never as a literal in command text or this report)
Created repl_test table and inserted baseline + pre-failover rows on node1, confirmed replication to node2/node3
Cloned node2 and node3 from node1 via pg_basebackup -R, started as standbys, confirmed pg_stat_replication streaming state and data on both
Simulated primary loss: stopped postgresql on node1
Promoted node2 to primary via pg_promote(), verified zero data loss, inserted a post-failover row to prove writability
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2 and restarted it; confirmed it streams from node2 with full data
Rebuilt node1 as a fresh standby of node2 via pg_basebackup (pg_rewind ruled out: data_checksums/wal_log_hints were off on source)
Captured boot_id and service/replication health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded ack), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and recovered standby state/data
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot, confirmed new boot_id and recovered standby state/data
Restarted node2 (primary) last after both standbys were healthy, confirmed new boot_id, primary role preserved, data intact, and both standbys reconnected streaming

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication established: node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys, data replicated
evidence.summary: node1 configured as primary with replicator role; node2 and node3 cloned via pg_basebackup and confirmed streaming/replaying with matching data and LSNs

evidence.requirement: Primary loss triggers standby promotion without losing committed data
evidence.summary: Pre-failover row confirmed replicated to both standbys before node1 was stopped; node2 promoted via pg_promote() and left the recovery state

evidence.requirement: New primary is writable and no committed data was lost
evidence.summary: Post-promotion INSERT on node2 succeeded and SELECT shows both pre-failover rows (id 1, 2) intact plus the new row

evidence.requirement: Surviving standby (node3) follows the new primary
evidence.summary: node3 repointed to node2, restarted, shown streaming from node2 in pg_stat_replication with all rows including the post-failover write

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) rejoins as standby of the current primary (node2)
evidence.summary: node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2, started as standby, confirmed pg_is_in_recovery=t, streaming state on node2, and full committed data present

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node1 boot identity changed and services/data recovered
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 71f12f87...; reboot acknowledged then node unreachable; post-reboot boot_id 30ce6106... (changed); postgresql active, standby recovery state true, all data present, node2 shows node1 streaming again

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node3 boot identity changed and services/data recovered
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b...; reboot acknowledged then unreachable; post-reboot boot_id 94657725... (changed); postgresql active, standby recovery state true, all data present, node2 shows node3 streaming again

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node2 (primary) boot identity changed and primary role/data/cluster quorum recovered
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bf8b9d80...; reboot acknowledged then unreachable; post-reboot boot_id 48298961... (changed); postgresql active with pg_is_in_recovery=f (still primary), all data intact, both node1 and node3 reconnected and streaming, confirming full 3-node cluster health after all restarts
